english.title: Fail to comply with a housing prohibition order
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), knowing that a prohibition order

(A)_[under section 20 of the Housing Act 2004 relating to a category 1 hazard, namely **(..SPECIFY HAZARD..),]_
(B)_[under section 21 of the Housing Act 2004 relating to a category 2 hazard, namely **(..SPECIFY HAZARD..),]_

had become operative in relation to specified premises, namely **(..SPECIFY PREMISES..), without reasonable excuse,

(C)_[used the premises]_
(D)_[permitted the premises to be used]_

in contravention of the order in that **(..SPECIFY CONTRAVENTION..)
english.legislation: Contrary to section 32 of the Housing Act 2004.
english.pointstoprove:
Date and Location
knowing that prohibition order had become operative in relation to premises
used premises in contravention of order OR
permitted the premises to be used in contravention of the order.

other.penalty:
Summary: A fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale and a further fine not exceeding £20 for every day or part of a day on which he/she so uses the premises, or permits them to be so used, after conviction.

Time limit for prosecutions:
6 months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
